basis: Systemic mycosis characteristically affects lungs and oral mucosa; destructive skin lesions occur in ~30-50%. Bone disease is uncommon.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: destructive oral mucosal infection is a characteristic, definition-level manifestation.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: persistent destructive cutaneous lesions occur in approximately 30-50%, near the inclusion threshold.

basis: Severe long-QT arrhythmia defines TS2; neurodevelopmental impairment occurs in >30%, probably over half. Syndactyly is absent; endocrine frequencies are uncertain.

decisions.neurologic: involved: neurodevelopmental impairment is common (>30%) but is not required to define this long-QT subtype.

basis: Copper disorder with defining neurologic disease and enteropathy; ichthyosis 6/6. Four-axis cap omits hearing loss 5/6, cholestasis 3/6 and cataract 2/6.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: persistent enteropathy is a defining syndrome component, with diarrhea in 6/6 and intestinal abnormalities in 80-99%.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: ichthyosis affects 6/6 and keratoderma 80-99%; retained as the fourth axis because primary labels are capped at three.

basis: Joubert brain malformation with developmental delay in 19/19; persistent eyelid dysfunction affects 15/18. Pulmonary, skeletal and renal abnormalities are below 30%.

decisions.ocular: involved: persistent ptosis in 15/18 represents loss of eyelid function; eyelids explicitly belong to the ocular axis.

basis: Inherited organelle disorder; persistent pigment loss or palmoplantar keratoderma affects most major subtypes (>30%). Blood, immune and neurologic defects vary across the group.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: persistent albinism or keratoderma is characteristic of the major subtypes and affects most patients across this umbrella.

basis: Purine disorder with defining neurodevelopmental abnormalities (80-99%); renal insufficiency and hearing loss each 30-79%. Gout and stones are separately diagnosed.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurodevelopmental anomalies explicitly define the severe early-onset subtype and occur in 80-99%.

basis: Most sellar neoplasms originate in the pituitary. CNS-origin subtypes and visual compression do not establish common neurologic or ocular damage across the umbrella.

decisions.neurologic: none: CNS-origin tumors form a minority of this predominantly pituitary umbrella; sellar location alone does not establish neural injury.

basis: Diabetic metabolic disease with defining retinal microvascular injury, hemorrhage and exudation; vascular injury is localized to the eye.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this is a diabetic metabolic disease, supported by its metabolic-disease ancestry; the metabolic mechanism axis applies.

basis: Historical G6PD-like locus without an established clinical phenotype; no evidence supports metabolic disease, G6PD deficiency or hemolysis.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: an enzyme-like locus name without a disease definition or phenotype does not establish a metabolic disorder.

basis: Glycolytic defect with defining hemolytic anemia and myopathy; neurodevelopmental impairment and ataxia occur in 30-79%. Renal and retinal damage occur in 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: myopathy is an explicitly defining manifestation of PGK deficiency; myopathy and rhabdomyolysis occur in 30-79%.
